title: Protecting Nonprofits from Catastrophic Cash Flow Strain Act of 2020
official_summary:
Protecting Nonprofits from Catastrophic Cash Flow Strain Act of 2020

This bill permits certain governmental entities, federally recognized tribes, and nonprofit organizations to make up front payments of 50% of unemployment benefits into the state Unemployment Trust Fund (in lieu of contributions) to be used exclusively to reduce such payments resulting from the COVID-19 (i.e., coronavirus disease 2019) pandemic.

Currently, the Department of Labor has issued guidance on April 27, 2020 (UIPL 18-20), requiring states to collect 100% of such payments up front and then reimburse them by 50% later.

In addition, the bill allows states to opt to issue such reimbursements or to reduce the amounts required to be paid for weeks of unemployment after March 12, 2020, and before enactment of this bill.

summary.headline: This law lets certain nonprofits, tribes, and government employers pay half of their unemployment costs up front to ease COVID-19 cash flow strain.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows certain governmental entities, federally recognized tribes, and nonprofit organizations to pay 50% of unemployment benefits up front into a state Unemployment Trust Fund, instead of the full amount that the Department of Labor's April 27, 2020 guidance required. The up-front payment can only be used to reduce unemployment payments caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. States may also choose to reimburse these employers or reduce the amounts they owe for weeks of unemployment after March 12, 2020 and before the law was enacted.

who_it_affects.how: They may pay 50% of their unemployment costs up front instead of the full amount under the earlier federal guidance.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a separate effective date, so it appears to take effect when the law was enacted on August 3, 2020.
